About Us
Zambia University College of Technology stands at the forefront of academic excellence, offering a diverse range of programs in engineering, technology, and business. Established with a vision to propel Zambia into the technological era, the university is committed to fostering a culture of innovation and cutting-edge education. Through rigorous academic curricula and state-of-the-art facilities, the institution aims to equip students with the skills and knowledge necessary to thrive in dynamic and rapidly evolving fields.
The university's significant contribution to the tech scene in Zambia has been pivotal in shaping the nation's technological landscape. By offering specialized programs in engineering and technology, Zambia University College of Technology has played a crucial role in addressing the demand for skilled professionals in these sectors. Graduates from the university have become key contributors to various industries, driving innovation, and leading transformative projects that contribute to the country's economic growth. The university's emphasis on practical, hands-on learning ensures that students are well-prepared to apply theoretical knowledge to real-world challenges.
Beyond academic pursuits, Zambia University College of Technology is renowned for its commitment to nurturing talent. The institution actively engages students in research, projects, and internships, providing them with opportunities to apply their skills in practical settings. Faculty members, with their industry experience, guide students in honing their talents, fostering a dynamic learning environment. Through mentorship programs and collaboration with industry leaders, the university creates a supportive ecosystem that encourages students to explore their potential, fostering a generation of skilled professionals ready to make significant contributions to Zambia's technological advancement.
Strategic Vision
To be a self-sustaining and leading higher learning institution in the provision of ICT programmes in the region that are responsive to emerging business and technological trends.
Mission Statement
To provide high quality training responsive to the needs of the market in the region and diversifying the business of the institution through innovation and consultancy services.

ZUT HACKERTRONS CROWNED NATIONAL CHAMPIONS AT 2026 DIGITAL SAFE ADVERS-AI CYBERSECURITY COMPETITION
9th November, 2026
Lusaka
The Zambia University College of Technology has recorded a historic achievement after its cybersecurity team, Hackertrons, emerged as overall national champions of the 2026 Digital Safe Advers-AI Capture The Flag (CTF) Competition, held on 31st October, 2026 at the University of Lusaka (UNILUS), Silverest Campus, Lusaka.
The five-member team secured K20,000 in prize money, while team captain Bibusa Nkolomba was named Top Hacker of the Competition, earning an additional K6,000 and bringing the team's combined winnings to K26,000.
The victory marks a significant milestone for ZUT, which has participated in the national competition for approximately four years, consistently reaching the finals but falling short of the championship.
This year, Hackertrons competed against participants from approximately 16 universities across Zambia. The team finished third in the online preliminary round held on 19th September, 2026, securing a place among the 10 universities that qualified for the national grand finale.
Following a series of demanding cybersecurity challenges that tested technical expertise, critical thinking and teamwork, Hackertrons emerged victorious, securing first position nationally.
The winning team comprised Bibusa Nkolomba (Team Captain), Obby Kalaluka, Mainza Namangani, Shadrick Chabala and Kabunda Katanga.
The students were accompanied by Mr. Dowson Sikute and Mr. Malambo, members of staff from the ICT Department's Cybersecurity section, who provided mentorship and technical support throughout the team's participation.
Five additional ZUT students, including first-year students, accompanied the team as supporters. Their participation provided valuable exposure to competitive cybersecurity and inspired interest in future competitions.
A notable aspect of the team's preparation was the development of KopaXploits, a student-built cybersecurity practice platform designed to support practical learning and skills development.
Accessible at https://kopaxploits.com , the platform provided Hackertrons with an opportunity to strengthen their technical competencies through continuous practice and problem-solving ahead of the competition.
Reflecting on the achievement, team captain Bibusa Nkolomba attributed the victory to sustained preparation, teamwork and the support received from fellow students and mentors. He also acknowledged the contribution of KopaXploits to the team's readiness.
The achievement highlights the ability of ZUT students to apply classroom knowledge in developing practical technological solutions while strengthening their competencies in cybersecurity.
The University further acknowledges the support provided by ZUT Management, under the leadership of the Acting Vice Chancellor, Dr. Betty Shitima Bweupe, whose encouragement and commitment contributed to the team's preparation and successful participation.
ZUT's contribution to the event extended beyond the competition, with Mr. Sikute, participating as an invited speaker. He delivered a presentation titled “Behind the Digital Evidence: The World of Digital Forensics,” highlighting the importance of digital forensics in modern cybersecurity practice.
The national championship represents an important milestone in ZUT's efforts to promote practical, industry-relevant education, innovation and technological excellence.
As Zambia continues to advance its digital transformation, the achievement underscores the role of higher learning institutions in developing skilled cybersecurity professionals capable of protecting digital infrastructure, responding to emerging cyber threats and contributing to national development.
The University congratulates Team Hackertrons on this historic achievement and commends all students and members of staff whose dedication contributed to the national victory.

ZUT CHALLENGES CLASS OF 2026 TO USE TECHNOLOGY AND INNOVATION TO DRIVE NATIONAL DEVELOPMENT
16th October 2026, Ndola
The Permanent Secretary - Education Services at the Ministry of Education, Dr. Kelvin Mambwe, has called on higher education institutions to extend quality assurance beyond regulatory compliance by investing in systems, teaching staff and infrastructure that equip graduates with professional competence and industry relevant skills.
Speaking at the 6th Graduation Ceremony held under the theme “Driving Sustainable Business Growth Through Innovation and Technology,” Dr. Mambwe reiterated that the Government of the Republic of Zambia recognizes education as the foundation for human capital development and economic transformation.
He acknowledged the university’s important role in developing the skills required across the technical and business sectors. He further urged the graduating students to embrace lifelong learning and continuous professional development to remain relevant in their respective industries and the ever-evolving world of work.
His Worship the Mayor of Ndola, Cllr. Kennedy Kasaba, was among the senior government officials who attended the 6th graduation ceremony of Zambia University College of Technology (ZUT).
The graduation ceremony was also attended by the Chief Executive Officer of the Higher Education Loans and Scholarships Board (HELSB), who witnessed the graduation of one of the Board’s members of staff, Mr Hector Simungala, who graduated with a Merit in Bachelor of Science in Information Technology.
The Board, Management and Staff of HELSB congratulate the Class of 2026 on this significant achievement and wish all graduates success as they embark on the next chapter of their professional journeys.
Zambia University College of Technology (ZUT) A/Vice Chancellor, Dr. Betty Shitima Bweupe, has challenged graduates to move beyond seeking employment and use their knowledge, skills and innovation to solve problems, create enterprises and contribute to Zambia’s economic development.
Speaking during the University’s 6th Convocation Graduation Ceremony held at the ZUT Main Campus in Ndola, The A/Vice Chancellor Dr. Betty Shitima Bweupe said ZUT remains committed to developing graduates capable of applying technology to address real-world challenges.
The ceremony was held under the theme “Driving Sustainable Business Growth through Innovation and Technology.”
The A/Vice Chancellor Dr. Betty Shitima Bweupe also highlighted the continued growth of the institution, noting that 712 graduands were celebrated at the 2026 ceremony, compared with 400 graduates at the 5th Graduation Ceremony in 2025.
She emphasised that the theme reflects ZUT’s conviction that technology must serve a purpose beyond itself and should be strategically applied to build resilient enterprises, improve productivity, strengthen industries and contribute to sustainable economic development.
She further noted that ZUT’s mandate aligns with the visionary leadership of the Government of the Republic of Zambia and the Grow Zambia Agenda under the stewardship of His Excellency, Mr. Hakainde Hichilema, President of the Republic of Zambia, which require skilled human capital capable of transforming technological concepts into practical solutions.
Through programmes in Information and Communication Technology, Engineering and Business, the University continues to equip students with competencies relevant to industry and national development.
The A/Vice Chancellor, Dr. Betty Shitima Bweupe also highlighted the University’s continued academic growth, including the introduction of the Bachelor of Science in Computer Science, Bachelor of Science in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence, Bachelor of Engineering in Industrial Automation and Control Systems and Bachelor of Digital Marketing.
She said ZUT had continued to record progress in research, innovation, practical training and international competitiveness.
Among the milestones highlighted were the University’s recognition as Second Best Training Service Provider at the 2026 Zambia International Trade Fair and Best Government Exhibit at the 2026 Zambia Agricultural and Commercial Show.
The A/Vice Chancellor further highlighted ZUT’s growing strategic partnerships with IIT Madras Zanzibar Campus, the National Remote Sensing Centre, Lusaka Telecoms Solutions, the Zambia Army and VCOM of China, which are helping strengthen the link between academic research and industry application.
In infrastructure development, ZUT completed a 350-seater lecture theatre and undertook upgrades to its campus-wide digital infrastructure. The number of students supported through the Higher Education Loans and Scholarships Board (HELSB) also increased from 573 in 2025 to 1,071 in 2026.
Addressing the Class of 2026, Dr. Bweupe encouraged the graduates to remain adaptable in an era increasingly shaped by Artificial Intelligence, cybersecurity and automation and to use their education to create value for society.
She said, "Class of 2026, go out there with confidence and humility. Use what you’ve learned to make a difference, solve problems with your ideas, and follow your passion to help the country thrive."
The 6th Graduation Ceremony brought together Government representatives, higher education institutions, industry partners, sponsors, parents, guardians and other stakeholders to celebrate the achievements of the Class of 2026.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
ZUT SIGNS LANDMARK MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH NATIONAL REMOTE SENSING CENTRE
23 July 2026 | Lusaka, Zambia
The Zambia University College of Technology (ZUT) has signed a landmark Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), marking another significant milestone in strengthening collaboration between academia and industry in advancing science, technology and innovation in Zambia.
The signing ceremony was held on 24 July 2026 in Lusaka.
Speaking during the ceremony, NRSC Executive Director, Dr. Patrick Sibanda, said that emerging technologies such as Earth observation, satellite systems, artificial intelligence, machine learning and big data are transforming the way governments and industries make decisions.
He emphasized that institutions of higher learning and industry must work together to produce graduates equipped with both theoretical knowledge and practical competencies required by today's technology-driven economy.
Dr. Sibanda noted that the specialised technologies and operations undertaken at the National Remote Sensing Centre are currently not taught at any university in Zambia, making collaboration with ZUT particularly important in developing the country's future workforce.
He further expressed satisfaction that the partnership had already begun yielding positive results even before the formal signing of the MoU.
"We are currently privileged to have students from the Zambia University College of Technology undertaking internship training at the National Remote Sensing Centre. What has been particularly impressive is that these students have gone beyond merely observing operations.
They have actively contributed innovative solutions that are already transforming aspects of our operations and demonstrating the immense value that young talent can bring when given the opportunity to work alongside industry professionals," said Dr. Sibanda.
Speaking at the same event, ZUT Acting Vice-Chancellor Dr. Betty Bweupe described the partnership as an important investment in Zambia's future scientists, engineers, innovators and technology leaders.
She stated that ZUT has already demonstrated the value of strong collaboration between academia and industry in driving innovation, strengthening human capital and accelerating national development.
Dr. Bweupe emphasized that this Memorandum of Understanding should translate into concrete outcomes, including collaborative curriculum development, joint research projects, innovation challenges, industrial attachments and internships, specialised training programmes and technology development initiatives that deliver measurable benefits for both institutions and the nation.
She further acknowledged that while the specialised expertise available at NRSC is not currently offered by any university in Zambia, ZUT is ready to embrace the challenge by working closely with the Centre to develop relevant curricula that respond to industry needs.
Zambia now hosts a specialised Ground Receiving Station, one of the country's most advanced scientific and engineering facilities, responsible for receiving, processing and disseminating Earth observation satellite data.
The partnership between ZUT and NRSC is expected to strengthen national capacity in space science, geospatial technologies and remote sensing while enhancing Zambia's competitiveness in the rapidly evolving global technology landscape.
The collaboration is also expected to establish a sustainable pipeline for identifying, developing and nurturing highly skilled graduates who will contribute to the continued growth of the National Remote Sensing Centre and the broader space and geospatial sector in Zambia.
The Memorandum of Understanding reinforces ZUT's commitment to building strategic partnerships that bridge academia and industry, foster innovation, and produce graduates equipped with the practical skills and technological expertise needed to drive Zambia's socio-economic transformation.

On 15th April 2026, a high-level delegation from the Zambia University College of Technology (ZUT) successfully concluded an official visit to the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras Zanzibar Campus in the United Republic of Tanzania.
This visit marks an important step in strengthening international collaboration and academic partnerships between the two institutions.

This initiative will greatly enhance staff development and strengthen ZUT’s research capacity.

Zambia University College of Technology expresses sincere appreciation to the leadership of IIT Madras Zanzibar for their warm hospitality and commitment to academic excellence.
This partnership is expected to play a transformative role in advancing staff development and contributing to the growth of the technological landscape in Zambia.

ZUT APPLICATION FEE PAYMENTS JUST GOT EASIER!
Published on , 12 Nov, 2026
Applying to the Zambia University College of Technology is now faster, easier and more convenient!
Prospective students can now pay their K150 application fee directly through the ZUT application portal using MTN MoMo, Zamtel Money or Airtel Money, in addition to the existing bank card and bank transfer options.
HOW TO PAY USING MOBILE MONEY
1️⃣ Log in to the ZUT application portal and select Pay Application Fee
2️⃣ Click Select Payment Option
3️⃣ Choose Mobile Money
4️⃣ Select your preferred mobile network
5️⃣ Enter your mobile money number
6️⃣ Approve the payment prompt on your phone by entering your Mobile Money PIN
✅ That's it! Your payment is complete once the transaction is confirmed.
Your journey towards a future in technology is now even more convenient!
Applications for the January 2027 Intake are open!
